title: Detroit-Style Pepperoni Pizza
subtitle: Crispy cheese edges, thick crust
description: Crispy cheese edges, thick crust. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Two 9x13 steel or dark cake pans

ingredients.name: Brick cheese or mild cheddar, shredded

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Detroit-Style Pepperoni Pizza in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch pork. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Mix and rise the dough
steps.instruction: Stir yeast into warm water with sugar; rest 5 minutes until foamy. Mix flour, salt, oil, and yeast water until a sticky dough forms. Knead 8 minutes. Rise covered 1–1½ hours until doubled — Detroit crust needs an airy, relaxed dough.

steps.title: Press into oiled pans
steps.instruction: Generously butter and oil two 9x13 steel or dark cake pans — not a round stone. Press dough into corners and up sides slightly. Do not stretch thin; Detroit is thick and airy.

steps.title: Cheese to the edges
steps.instruction: Scatter cheese edge-to-edge so it touches the pan walls — this creates the frico crispy cheese skirt. Top with pepperoni if using. Rest 15–20 minutes while the oven preheats to 550°F or your oven max on the bottom rack.

steps.title: First bake
steps.instruction: Bake on the bottom rack 12–14 minutes until cheese caramelizes at the edges and the bottom sounds hollow when tapped. Edges should look fried, not pale.

steps.title: Sauce stripes on top
steps.instruction: Whisk crushed tomatoes with oregano and garlic powder. Remove pizza from oven and spoon sauce in two or three lengthwise stripes ON TOP of the baked cheese — Detroit puts sauce after the bake. Return to oven 5–7 minutes.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F with a 3-minute rest. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Detroit-Style Pepperoni Pizza onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Rest and cut rectangles
steps.instruction: Rest 5 minutes, then cut into rectangular slices with a bench scraper. Serve on sheet trays — crispy cheese edges face out so the crew sees the Detroit signature.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Cut Detroit pies into rectangles so crispy cheese edges face out — that is the signature.
Serve from sheet trays, not round pie servers — these are 9x13 pan pizzas.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Crispy cheese edges, thick crust. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Detroit-Style Pepperoni Pizza runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
